content.text:
I submitted index 15 (Mn 0.595 / Sr 0.405), which had the highest photocurrent of the three measurements: 1.41 µA. That used the whole merit budget. I made no XRD measurements, so which crystal phase each film contains was never checked. The phase links below are inferred from composition alone.

| Index | Mn fraction | Photocurrent | Why I picked it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 25 | 0.44 | 0.24 µA | Near Sr4Mn3O10, which has the widest predicted band gap in this system (1.92 eV) |
| 20 | 0.50 | 0.70 µA | Near SrMnO3, predicted gap 1.79 eV |
| **15** | **0.595** | **1.41 µA** | Near Sr3Mn4O12 (predicted gap 1.09 eV) and the Gaussian-process model's top predicted value |

Photocurrent went up at every step towards the Mn-rich end, even though the predicted band gaps got narrower. So the best film in the library may be even more Mn-rich than index 15, for example indices 16, 13 or the Mn 0.70–0.86 range. None of those were measured, so index 15 is only the best of what I tested. The Sr-rich end (Mn below 0.4) looks unlikely to be better: photocurrent fell as Sr increased, and the phases there are predicted to be near-metallic.
